title: Connection pool exhaustion: a holder that talks to the network and does no work

problem.summary: Something opens connections to a datastore and holds them without using them. In the kernel it shows as a container whose events are almost all network and ioctl, with no locking and almost no CPU.
symptoms: callers of one datastore start failing or timing out
the datastore itself is not busy
the failure is about availability of connections, not latency

discriminators.not_this_problem: ioctl does not appear at all in any other family measured - 0.0% for lock contention, deadlock, priority inversion, both stress families and the network fault
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED on 41 labelled runs across 8 families with blueprints/lib/fingerprint_table.py (22-09-2026). conn_pool_exhaustion 17.3% (n=5); every other family measured 0.0-0.4%. This is the cleanest single separation in the table.

discriminators.this_problem: network 35.6% and futex 0.0% (n=5) - it talks, it does not lock
discriminators.not_this_problem: the delayed-ack fault also carries network (17.9%) but with 25.8% futex alongside it
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED on 41 labelled runs across 8 families with blueprints/lib/fingerprint_table.py (22-09-2026). network 35.6% / futex 0.0% (n=5) against 17.9% / 25.8% for nagle_delayed_ack (n=5).

discriminators.signal: it is nearly idle for the work it appears to be doing
discriminators.this_problem: 545-550 events/s with on-CPU at 3.2% (n=5) - holding, not working
discriminators.not_this_problem: a busy client would show far more on-CPU time
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED on 41 labelled runs across 8 families with blueprints/lib/fingerprint_table.py (22-09-2026). 545-550 events/s (n=5), a spread of under 1% across five runs, with on_cpu 3.2%.

unverified_do_not_claim.claim: the exhausted pool can be seen from the datastore side
unverified_do_not_claim.measurement: we measured the holder container only. Whether the datastore's own container shows a matching signature was not tested.
unverified_do_not_claim.consequence: do not claim it. Name the holder, not the victim.

reproduction.teardown: the recipe restores state; verify against /sys/fs/cgroup
harness_only: the fault is injected as a sidecar container, which is a property of our harness. In production the same mechanism occurs inside an existing service - so the SHAPE transfers, the newcomer shortcut does not

collection_order.why_these: MEASURED BASIS. Every discriminator in this blueprint is a share of these event groups within one container. Nothing else in the trace is required, and no other modality is used - this blueprint was built and validated on kernel traces alone.

processing.expect: a CTF directory with metadata and channel streams

processing.step: Find containers that are active during the window and absent before it
processing.expect: one container with substantial traffic during the window and none before. If none appears, this blueprint does not apply - say so and stop

processing.step: Measure what share of its own events that container spends on each kind of work
processing.expect: the share profile below, within the measured range

processing.step: Apply the rules and emit the verdict
processing.expect: a verdict naming the container and the mechanism, or an explicit abstain
one page showing the shares, the cut, and what was ruled out

outputs.contains: culprit container pid_ns, its event shares, and the shares of every other container for comparison
per-container event shares for the window
each family's measured share on the deciding axis, with this run's value marked

verdict_when: a container is new to the window
its share profile matches the measured range below
no sibling container shows the same profile

rule_out.when: network is present but futex is around 26% rather than 0%
no container is new to the window and the datastore itself is slow

decision.root_cause_is: the container holding connections open against the datastore

provenance.authored_by: measured from StrataTrace v2 kernel traces
provenance.notes: Built 22-09-2026 from blueprints/lib/fingerprint_table.py over 41 labelled runs of 8 families. Candidate signals were first put through discover_signature.py (a specificity sweep across families, which rejected unlinkat, ftruncate, block_split, lseek and dup as window artefacts) and who_makes_it.py (which rejected the nagle_delayed_ack host-wide signal as 94% our own load generator). KERNEL TRACES ONLY - no metrics, logs or spans were consulted.

apply_when: callers of a datastore fail or time out while the datastore is idle
the symptom is about connection availability, not query latency
do_not_apply_when: the datastore is itself busy or slow - see db-latency-dependency-wait
no container is new to the window
applicability.cheap_precheck: a container appeared whose events are mostly network and ioctl, with no futex at all

stopping_conditions.conclude: the share profile matches and no sibling container matches it too
stopping_conditions.stop_and_switch: a discriminating share falls outside its measured range
stopping_conditions.stop_insufficient: no container is new to the window and none stands out

applicable_symptoms: callers of one datastore start failing or timing out
the datastore itself is not busy
the failure is about availability of connections, not latency

historical_effectiveness.note: shares measured on 5 runs of this family

evidence_sufficiency.if_below_floor: report the shares and say which blueprint they sit between
evidence_sufficiency.report_when_stuck: the container's shares and every sibling's, side by side
